key_insight: Learning physically interpretable fractional-step operators separately reduces fluid-flow rollout error compared with a single full-step neural operator.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports fast CFD surrogates for varied geometries, with approximately 1,000× faster per-step inference than the Monte Carlo solver at comparable error levels.
method: Decompose each time step and train separate operators using intermediate solver states.
Use conditional-linear Fourier neural operators with linear state mappings conditioned nonlinearly on inputs such as geometry.
Apply symmetry sampling and corrective cycling to limit autoregressive error accumulation.
evidence_signal: Experiments on 2D and 3D flows with varying geometries and initial conditions report 68% and 40% lower mean relative L2 rollout error, respectively, versus a single full-step neural operator.
watch_item: Training requires intermediate solver states; generalization beyond the evaluated geometries and flow conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Neural Operator Splitting for Fluid Dynamics in Complex Geometry
